newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Truce expires in Chittagong Hill Tracts.
newsitem.headline: Truce expires in Chittagong Hill Tracts.

text.p: A truce between the government and separatist tribal rebels in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts expired on Thursday, officials said on Friday.

"We have received no communication or request from the rebel Shanti Bahini (peace force) for an extension of the truce, which expired at midnight. So it's over now," one Hill Tracts official told reporters.
The truce had been extended for one month each time since early this year while both sides agreed to hold peace talks, although they produced no agreement.
"But suddenly the Shanti Bahini and its political wing Parbatya Chattagram Janasanghati Samily (PCJSS) have gone quiet," the official said.
The government would not make any pleas to the rebels but would strengthen counter-insurgency operations, he said without elaborating.
The insurgency began in 1973 after Bangladesh rejected Shanti Bahini's demand for autonomy for the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma.
It also wants expulsion of some 300,000 non-tribal settlers from the region.
Officials say over 8,500 people including rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which has also forced thousands of tribal families to seek refuge in India.
